Polish Engineering Sector Sees Innovation with New Modular Bridge System Launch

Warsaw, June 12—Poland’s engineering and construction industry marked a significant milestone today with the launch of a new modular bridge system developed by Kraków-based Innovatebuild S.A. The product, designed to accelerate infrastructure development, was unveiled at the annual Polish Construction Forum in Warsaw.

Innovatebuild’s CEO, Marta Kaczmarek, emphasized the benefits for both urban and rural regions. “Our modular bridge system enables rapid assembly and disassembly, reducing construction time by up to 40% compared to traditional methods,” Kaczmarek said. “This innovation supports the government’s push to modernize transport links across Poland.”

The launch comes as Poland continues to invest heavily in infrastructure, with the Ministry of Development and Technology allocating over PLN 30 billion for road and bridge upgrades in 2024. Trade association Polskie Stowarzyszenie Inżynierów Budownictwa welcomed the development, noting that efficient solutions are vital amid growing demand for resilient, sustainable infrastructure.

“The modular approach addresses challenges like workforce shortages and material costs,” said Tomasz Urbanek, the association’s spokesperson. “It’s a timely response to the sector’s needs.”

Analysts at Varsovia Capital noted the potential export opportunities, citing interest from regional partners in Central and Eastern Europe. “Polish engineering firms are increasingly recognized for innovation in infrastructure,” said analyst Ewa Zielińska.

Innovatebuild expects to begin pilot installations this summer in the Mazowieckie and Podlaskie regions. The company projects that the system could serve both public and private sector clients, with initial capacity to deliver components for up to 50 bridge projects annually.
